-- OpenStackSplitFrame(maxStack, owner, anchor, anchorTo) — ref StackSplitFrame.lua:2-24, -- verbatim shape. `owner` must already carry `owner.SplitStack = function(owner, n) ... end` -- (BagFrame.xml's `BenillaBagSlot_OnClick` sets it right before calling this, mirroring -- ContainerFrameItemButton_OnClick's own closure). maxStack < 2 hides instead of showing (a -- 1-stack has nothing to split) — the ref's own guard. function OpenStackSplitFrame(maxStack, owner, anchor, anchorTo) local frame = StackSplitFrame if frame.owner then frame.owner.hasStackSplit = nil end frame.maxStack = maxStack if frame.maxStack < 2 then frame:Hide() return end frame.owner = owner owner.hasStackSplit = true frame.split = 1 -- `typed` distinguishes "1 because nothing has been typed yet" from "1 because the -- player typed it": the first digit REPLACES the seed, later digits append. Cleared on -- every open, so a dialog reopened after typing starts fresh. frame.typed = nil StackSplitText:SetText(frame.split) StackSplitLeftButton:Disable() StackSplitRightButton:Enable() -- ref l.21-22: ClearAllPoints first — SetPoint only replaces an anchor of the SAME -- point, and the anchor callers choose (BagFrame.xml passes "BOTTOMRIGHT") differs from -- this frame's authored placeholder ("CENTER"), so skipping this would leave both live. frame:ClearAllPoints() frame:SetPoint(anchor, owner, anchorTo, 0, 0) frame:Show() end
-- UpdateStackSplitFrame(maxStack) — ref l.26-52: the owner's stack shrank/grew out from -- under an OPEN spinner (e.g. a server correction). Not called by anything in benilla yet -- (no caller has a live reason to resize an open spinner today) — kept so a later caller -- (the paper doll / bank slice) drops in without a new function. function UpdateStackSplitFrame(maxStack) local frame = StackSplitFrame frame.maxStack = maxStack if frame.maxStack < 2 then if frame.owner then frame.owner.hasStackSplit = nil end frame:Hide() return end if frame.split > frame.maxStack then frame.split = frame.maxStack StackSplitText:SetText(frame.split) end if frame.split == frame.maxStack then StackSplitRightButton:Disable() else StackSplitRightButton:Enable() end if frame.split == 1 then StackSplitLeftButton:Disable() else StackSplitLeftButton:Enable() end end
-- The arrows go through the shared setter (below) rather than nudging the count and the -- two buttons themselves: with typed entry live there are now three writers of -- `frame.split`, and three copies of the enable/disable rule is how they drift apart. function BenillaStackSplitLeft_Click() BenillaStackSplitSet(StackSplitFrame.split - 1) end
function BenillaStackSplitRight_Click() BenillaStackSplitSet(StackSplitFrame.split + 1) end
function BenillaStackSplitOkay_Click() local frame = StackSplitFrame if frame.owner then frame.owner.SplitStack(frame.owner, frame.split) end frame:Hide() end
function BenillaStackSplitCancel_Click() StackSplitFrame:Hide() end
-- The one place the count is written, so the buttons' enable state and the label can -- never disagree with `frame.split` (the arrow handlers below call it too). Clamped to -- [1, maxStack] because every caller can overshoot: typing 9 into a 5-stack, or the -- arrows at their ends. function BenillaStackSplitSet(n) local frame = StackSplitFrame if n < 1 then n = 1 end if n > frame.maxStack then n = frame.maxStack end frame.split = n StackSplitText:SetText(n) if n <= 1 then StackSplitLeftButton:Disable() else StackSplitLeftButton:Enable() end if n >= frame.maxStack then StackSplitRightButton:Disable() else StackSplitRightButton:Enable() end end
-- Typed digits (decision 1319). The engine hands OnChar the literal character, so this is -- a digit test and an append: the first keystroke replaces the seeded 1, each later one -- shifts a decimal place in. A digit that would overshoot the stack is CLAMPED rather than -- rejected -- typing 9 against a 5-stack leaves 5, which is what the player meant -- and -- clamping keeps `typed` set, so a following digit still appends against the clamp. -- Anything that is not a digit is ignored here; the frame consumes the key regardless -- (the engine's existence gate decides that, not this handler's return). function StackSplitFrame_OnChar() local c = arg1 if c < "0" or c > "9" then return end local frame = StackSplitFrame local digit = tonumber(c) local n if frame.typed then n = frame.split * 10 + digit else n = digit end -- A leading 0 types nothing: the count can never be 0, so it stays 1 and unlatched, -- and the next digit still reads as the first one. if n < 1 then return end frame.typed = true BenillaStackSplitSet(n) end
-- The editing/commit keys for typed entry. BACKSPACE drops the last digit (and unlatches -- at the end, so the next digit starts over rather than appending to a stale 1); ENTER -- commits exactly as Okay does and ESCAPE cancels, which is what a player expects of a -- dialog they are typing into. The arrow keys drive the spinner. Every other key is -- swallowed by the frame -- the reference's own consequence of having a key script bound -- at all, and the reason this dialog must not stay open invisibly. function StackSplitFrame_OnKeyDown() local key = arg1 local frame = StackSplitFrame if key == "BACKSPACE" then local n = floor(frame.split / 10) if n < 1 then frame.typed = nil BenillaStackSplitSet(1) else BenillaStackSplitSet(n) end elseif key == "ENTER" then BenillaStackSplitOkay_Click() elseif key == "ESCAPE" then BenillaStackSplitCancel_Click() elseif key == "LEFT" then BenillaStackSplitLeft_Click() elseif key == "RIGHT" then BenillaStackSplitRight_Click() end end
-- OnHide (ref l.158-162): ANY hide — Okay, Cancel, or ToggleGameMenu's chain hook below — -- clears the owner's `hasStackSplit` flag (ref ItemButtonTemplate's OnHide, ContainerFrame.xml -- l.35-39, checks `this.hasStackSplit` to auto-close the spinner if the SLOT itself goes away -- mid-split — no consumer needs that half here, but the flag's own clear is this function's -- job regardless of which button caused the hide). function StackSplitFrame_OnHide() local frame = StackSplitFrame if frame.owner then frame.owner.hasStackSplit = nil end end
